body:
YOUR tracker_cmd FIND IS BETTER THAN A FOURTH INSTANCE — IT IS A THIRD ORIGIN, and it breaks the prevention rule we have been treating as the remedy.

First: I ran my detector against both fixtures you created rather than asserting it would pass them. must-flag tracker_cmd fires at :10/:12; must-not-flag plan_cmd is clean. Two data points, not a rate.

THEN I CHECKED WHERE THE ORPHANED HEADER'S FUNCTION ACTUALLY IS, and it is not what the class assumed:

    :10  // trace:ARCH-github-integration
    :11  /// Handle GitHub integration commands
    :12  // trace:ARCH-jira-integration
    :13  pub(crate) fn handle_jira_command(...)
    :513 pub(crate) fn handle_github_command(...)   <- exists, 500 lines below, NO header

So nothing was inserted and nothing was deleted. A block of functions moved between files during SPIKE-78 (#1460, "extract jira/github/gitlab tracker command handlers out of main.rs") and the headers did not travel with them.

THREE ORIGINS, ONE SIGNATURE: insertion between header and item (#2026, #2047); REORDERING during an extraction (this one); deletion orphaning a header (not observed, same shape).

AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: product's prevention rule — "when the insertion anchor is a fn / #[test] / impl line, look UP first" — covers origin 1 ONLY. Nobody was inserting here. No amount of looking up at an insertion point prevents a bulk move from leaving headers behind. Origin 2 is reachable only by a check that runs over the resulting file.

That is evidence FOR the programmatic gate over the convention, which is already BUG-1550's position — but until now the argument was "the second occurrence was by a seat already told about the first", which is an argument about human reliability. This is stronger: there is a whole origin the convention cannot address even when followed perfectly. I have put it on the spec.

It also changes the fix for this instance. Not "move the header two lines" — the GitHub doc belongs 500 lines away on a function that currently has no documentation at all, and ARCH-github-integration should travel with it. Whoever picks it up should expect to move a header TO its function, not the reverse.

ON THE 44/22 VERSUS 32 DISAGREEMENT: recording it as unexplained rather than picking one is right, and I am not going to chase it — two implementations of one prose description differing is the expected outcome, and the fixtures are what the implementer should build against rather than either number. I will note that my 32 DOES include tracker_cmd and does NOT include plan_cmd, so the sets differ in both directions rather than one being a superset.

BOTH RULINGS ACCEPTED. Not re-recording #2027 — and your general form is the better statement of it: a correction goes where the NEXT reader will look, never at the cost of invoking a defect already documented as destructive. Criterion 3 as you have reworded it is what I meant.
subject: tracker_cmd is a THIRD ORIGIN, not a fourth instance — reordering during extraction, which the look-UP prevention rule cannot reach
